findings.description: PatientProfile wraps Patient with 12 getter/setter methods that directly delegate to fields without adding logic, making its interface nearly as complex as the underlying data—clients pay the cost of wrapper instantiation and method calls for direct field access.
export.ts has no logic of its own, only selecting between renderText and renderHtml based on format, adding indirection without consolidation—handlers could import renderer directly.

Test helper functions recent() and byEntity() read directly from the memory array implementation detail, bypassing the AuditSink abstraction and preventing true replacement of the audit backend in testing scenarios.

Notice numbering is split across four trivial modules (1–3 lines each) that must be coordinated to understand how notice numbers are generated; consolidating to a single NoticeNumbering module with a simpler public interface would eliminate bouncing between files.

MemberStore returns raw QueryResult objects, forcing MemberService to repeatedly check rowCount and convert rows to domain types in get(), updateContact(), and card(); raising the store's abstraction level to return domain objects or throw would eliminate boilerplate and match LoanStore's pattern.

LoanGateway is a pure pass-through proxy whose methods directly forward to identically-named LoanStore methods; removing it or giving it real responsibility would clarify whether the persistence layer needs indirection.
Global settings() calls throughout business logic create tight coupling to configuration with module-level caching that blocks per-instance configuration and complicates testing.
Services implicitly record audit events via global sink with useAuditSink() injection, hiding audit as a dependency and forcing test mocks even when audit behavior is not the test's concern.
Paging validation logic duplicated identically in middleware.paging() and order/service.validatePaging(); changes to validation rules require updates in both places.

Pricing and bill-building modules have circular imports: pricing imports describeLine from builder while builder imports priceOf, lineTotal, roundMoney, and pricedLines from pricing; resolving this cycle would clarify separation between domain pricing logic and presentation-layer bill construction.

Patient contact normalization and formatting is scattered across four single-function modules, all imported and used together in service.ts; consolidating into a single contact handling module would reduce import coupling and navigation friction.
Pagination validation rules are duplicated across middleware extraction (paging) and service-layer validation (validatePaging), requiring updates in two places if constraints change.
Config class has 12+ thin getter methods that forward directly to Settings object; deepening would eliminate the wrapper or group related settings into sub-objects.

Payment due date calculation is scattered across four files with four different implementations (varying in timezone, business-day vs calendar-day, weekend handling), making consistent changes to payment terms hard.
Invoice.dueAt is calculated by simple date arithmetic in builder, but renderer recalculates payBy() skipping weekends, risking mismatch between stored and displayed due date.

Global mutable counters (sequence, lastNumber) in newId() and nextNumber() create side effects preventing parallel test execution; extracting the counter as an injectable dependency would localize the logic.
Settings accessed directly via global settings() calls from 8 modules across layers; injecting configuration would eliminate coupling and put settings access behind a smaller interface.
Pricing logic (priceOf, lineTotal, formatAmount) spread across service, invoice builder, and handlers; consolidating into a pricing service would localize pricing changes.
Module-level sequence counters for ID generation (lastNumber, sequence) are not resettable or thread-safe; injecting ID strategies would make these testable and distributable.

Pricing imports describeLine from bill builder; builder imports pricing calculations from pricing—circular dependency couples billing and pricing logic tightly.
Patient contact logic—normalization and display—fragmented across four single-function modules; consolidating would unify the concept behind one interface.
Pagination validation logic duplicated identically in middleware and service layer; changes to validation rules must be made in two places.

Driver active status determined with inconsistent grace periods (7 days in service, 1 day in handler, 0 days in scheduler), plus unused isActiveDriver() function, forcing logic changes across three modules.

Manifest export audit method exists but is never called from handler, requiring handler modification to instrument—no service layer to mediate.

PatientProfile is a pure wrapper class with only getter/setter pass-throughs; displayName creates it just to read one field, and the handler creates it to extract all fields via method calls, forcing unnecessary object allocation and indirection.
Paging validation rules (offset ≥ 0, limit > 0, clamp to max) are duplicated across two modules; changing validation requirements touches both files and risks divergence.

The Config class wraps Settings with twelve getter methods that add ceremony without value; the interface is nearly as complex as the underlying data, forcing changes across ten modules when config structure changes.

findings.description: Loan status concept is scattered across five modules (type definition, valid states, transition rules, terminal-state check, display labels); understanding the status model requires bouncing between all of them.
The audit module's write() function has a hidden side effect: recording a 'cancelled' action triggers reminder scheduling, coupling two concerns and leaking behavior across the audit boundary.
Row-to-domain conversion for Loan is duplicated: fromRow() is defined in service.ts but reminders.ts repeats the same mapping inline, forcing schema changes to be applied in two places.

Settings dependency spreads across 10+ modules each calling global settings() for different config subsets; injecting settings into service/handler constructors would make dependencies explicit and allow partial configuration per layer.

Paging validation is duplicated: middleware.paging() validates, then handler passes result to service.list() which re-validates with validatePaging(); removing service-layer validation would clarify the boundary and eliminate redundant logic.

Audit recording happens as a fire-and-forget side effect with global state, making it difficult to test in isolation and creating asymmetric error handling (disabled silently succeeds, failures propagate); injecting an Auditor dependency would make testing explicit and error handling clear.

Manifest number generation relies on module-level lastNumber counter with no reset function, causing non-deterministic test behavior and non-reproducible manifests across restarts; generating from trip ID or timestamp would be deterministic and testable.
